f.prompt_g03: a photograph of a lighthouse on a cliff at sunset
f.prompt_x07: a white mug on a desk with the word HELLO printed on it
f.cfg_story: Across the sweep, accuracy rises from 77.8% at s = 1 to 96.4% at s = 5 and falls back to 78.3% at 15; FD is best at s = 2 (35.5, better than DDPM at 1,000 steps) and worsens beyond it as samples become bolder and more alike: diversity falls at every step up (28.38 to 20.28), and pixels at full white grow from 3.4% to 35.5%, the grey-scale version of over-saturation. At s = 0 (no label at all) only 10.8% match the requested class, about chance.
f.sd_cfg_note: Read across the row: the empty prompt draws an unrelated indoor scene; s = 1 a sunset coast with no clear lighthouse; from s = 2 the lighthouse is there; past 10 the sky turns deep orange and contrast hardens (mean saturation 0.35 at s = 1, 0.47 at 7.5, 0.61 at 20). Scales of 1 or less ran one U-Net pass per step (8.5 s per image) against two above 1 (15.8 s).
f.sd_x07_note: None of the four puts the word on the mug: the text lands on a card beside it. At s = 1 the letters are garbled; at 4 and 7.5 the word reads HELLO (with an added exclamation mark at 7.5); at 15 a heart replaces the O. Guidance made the word legible, not correctly placed: binding text to an object is a limit of the CLIP text encoder and the model, which more guidance does not fix.
